ROUND 10, BOUNDED, and every change is a deletion or a narrowing. (1) |N BLOCK HEADERS REFUSED. The header regex accepted an explicit indentation indicator and the body baseline was then taken from the FIRST CONTENT LINE rather than the indicator, so a first line indented deeper than the indicator set a baseline every later line fell short of, and every later line closed the block: `run: |2` with a 14-space first line and a 12-space second parsed as "npm run test:gate" and returned [], while PyYAML 6.0.3 gives "    npm run test:gate
  && npm run some:unreviewed:step
". MEASURED IDENTICALLY ON main (7f7bddd) AND ON ROUND 9 (bff6bbe), so this is older than Wave 1 and this branch did not introduce it — the round-9 reviewer predicted it was new, ran the pre-image, and reported its own prediction wrong. `>2`, `|2+` and `|-2` do the same; `|9` is invalid YAML outright. Refused rather than honoured: one more deletion, not one more model, which is the stop condition this function is held to. CHOMPING STAYS READ and I verified that myself rather than inheriting it: `|-` and `|+` change only the TRAILING newline (measured: `|-` gives `npm run a
&& npm run b`, `|+` the same plus a trailing newline) and a trailing newline is not a second command; both produce the identical finding on both trees, and refusing them would cost the escape hatch that makes every other refusal free. (2) THE FALSE 'unguarded' FINDING IS FIXED, AND I CORRECT MY OWN PROVENANCE CLAIM: `if: "${{ !cancelled() }}"` is a CORRECTLY GUARDED step written with quotes; the quoted scalar is refused (deliberately) and left raw, so a plain `s.if !== CI_GUARD` test ALSO reported it as carrying no guard — one true finding and one false one about the same line, the false one saying the opposite of what is there. But main reports that step unguarded TOO, measured, so this is NOT a defect the round-9 deletion introduced: round 8 masked it as a side effect of unquoting every scalar and deleting the decode took the mask away. NOT FAIL-OPEN: a refused `if:` is itself a blocking ciChainFindings finding, so `if: "${{ always() }}"` — quoted AND weakened — still fails the build, once, with a true message. The predicate was spelled TWICE in the test file so the fix had to land in both or they would disagree about the same workflow; it is unguardedSteps() in the library now, spelled once, exported, and its guard parameter is mutated. (3) THE JSDoc CLAIMED 'The escape hatch is total.' The hatch is total; the READING of it was not, which is precisely what the |N hole proves — a sentence overstating what is enforced, sitting inside the argument the whole refusal rests on. Split into the claim and the check. (5) ciRunCommands KEEPS refused text, decided by measurement: a refused step already produces a BLOCKING ciChainFindings finding against the REAL allowlist (verified by planting one in the real ci.yml — 1 finding), so the runner-ban's view of refused text is unreachable in a workflow that can merge; excluding would make the ban blind on text it currently half-sees, for nothing, and in the continuation case both options give 0 hits anyway.
